title: SAT Reading and Writing — Practice Mock 1

questions.question: Passage: Urban heat islands. As used in the passage, the word mitigation most nearly means
options: complete elimination
reduction of severity
scientific measurement
public celebration

questions.question: Passage: Urban heat islands. One reason cities are hotter than nearby rural areas is that cities
options: receive more direct sunlight year-round
have less vegetation to support evaporative cooling
are located at lower elevations
experience stronger ocean winds

questions.question: Passage: Green roofs. Which choice best describes the function of the paragraph about green roofs?
options: It introduces a potential solution and summarizes research findings.
It disputes the existence of urban heat islands.
It compares green roofs with solar panels.
It defines transpiration for a general audience.

questions.question: Passage: Green roofs. Stormwater is mentioned primarily to
options: argue that sewers should be replaced
identify an additional benefit of green roofs
explain why irrigation is unnecessary
criticize municipal tax credits

questions.question: Passage: Green roofs. Which statement is best supported?
options: Green roofs always pay for themselves within one year.
Structural engineering limits where green roofs can be installed.
Toronto has banned conventional roofing materials.
Heat islands occur only in tropical climates.

questions.question: Passage: Policy. Effective urban cooling policy should be
options: limited to rooftop vegetation
abandoned in favor of air conditioning
combined across building and city scales
applied only during heat waves

questions.question: Although maintenance costs deter some owners, cities that offer incentives may see adoption rise because ____.
options: incentives offset part of the upfront expense
rural areas lack pavement
transpiration stops at night
heat islands cool without vegetation

questions.question: Which detail best shows that green-roof results are not uniform?
options: Many cities experience higher temperatures than surrounding rural areas.
Results vary with plant species, soil depth, and irrigation.
Scientists caution that green roofs alone cannot eliminate heat islands.
Building-scale interventions offer visible benefits.
